title: Extended assessment criteria
subject: History
unit: Spring 2: The Second World War, Churchill and the Holocaust
source: Written for history/y9 lesson 11 (Extended assessment criteria (portal printable; assessed))
intro: Lesson 11: Justice and remembrance; our extended assessment. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Perpetrators, bystanders, rescuers
points: Perpetrators: ordered or carried out crimes

model.title: Why should the Holocaust be remembered? Plan

parts.text: Para 1: to honour the victims as individuals
Para 2: to understand how hatred grows step by step
Para 3: to recognise and prevent genocide today (Srebrenica)
Conclusion: remembrance is a duty and a warning

keywords.def: a person who commits a crime
someone who sees wrong and does nothing
keeping the memory of people and events alive
deliberate killing of a whole people

questions.q: Explain why the Nuremberg trials were important. (2 marks)
questions.a: Leaders were held responsible under international law (1); 'following orders' was not accepted as an excuse (1)

questions.q: Core (assessed): In the portal response box, write the extended assessment: 'Why should the Holocaust be remembered, and how should we remember it?'
questions.a: Assessed: knowledge 1933 to 1945, explanation, argument, judgement

questions.q: Extend: Add a paragraph on the Second World War context: how war made genocide easier to hide.
questions.a: War, conquered lands in the East, secrecy

questions.q: Holocaust Memorial Day is held on:
questions.a: B) 27 January. 27 January marks the liberation of Auschwitz in 1945.

questions.q: Big question: how should the world remember the Holocaust?
questions.a: By honouring victims, teaching how it happened, and acting against hatred and genocide today
